newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Exiled king hails move to restore citizenship.
newsitem.headline: Exiled king hails move to restore citizenship.

text.p: Romania's exiled King Michael, who lives in Switzerland, on Wednesday hailed a decision by Bucharest's new centrist leaders to restore his citizenship, stripped from him by communist rulers 48 years ago.

Michael was "extremely pleased" by Bucharest's gesture, a spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone from his residence at Versoix, Switzerland. "It is another signal as to how much Romania has changed since the last elections," she said. "This as an act of justice for the entire period of communist dictatorship."
The coalition government led by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea promised on Wednesday swift action to redress the communist-era wrong done to Michael.

"The Romanian government will take urgent steps to scrap the arbitrary decision of 1948," a government statement said. Royalists and leading Romanian intellectuals had called for Michael's rights as a Romanian citizen to be restored.
"The Justice Ministry will present to the government a
solution in order to repair the injustice done by the Communists in 1948," the statement said.
Michael, now 75, was dethroned and bundled into exile in 1947 by Moscow-backed Communists who seized power after World War Two. They stripped him of his citizenship one year later.
In a break from the stand taken by previous post-communist governments on the former monarch, the government used his former official title of "King Michael I" in Wednesday's statement.
The former ruling leftists, who were thrown out of office in presidential and general elections last November, had insisted on referring to Michael as "the ex-King".
Michael was feted by hundreds of thousands of well-wishers during an emotional Orthodox Easter homecoming in 1992.

His subsequent homecoming attempts were thwarted by then-president Ion Iliescu's leftist supporters, who conditioned a visa for Michael on his recognition of the post-communist constitution of 1991 which defines Romania as a republic.
Iliescu had painted his centrist rival Emil Constantinescu as a closet monarchist during last November's elections, in a desperate bid to maintain his seven-year grip on power.
Michael hailed the reformers' victory over ex-communists in the polls three months ago and pledged to defend his country's interest worldwide.
